title: Birational locally finitely presented separated maps are isomorphisms over a dense open
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism] that is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $X$ and $Y$ each have finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] and $f$ is birational: it maps the generic points of the irreducible components of $Y$ bijectively onto those of $X$ [def-sc-generic-point], and the induced homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,f(\eta)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ is an isomorphism for each such $\eta$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then there is a dense open subset $V\subseteq X$ such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, morphisms-lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open, separated and locally finitely presented case

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-birational-common-dense-opens] to $f$. Its finite-component, locally-finite-presentation and generic-local-ring hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here; it requires no reducedness. Obtain dense open subschemes $U\subseteq Y$ and $V\subseteq X$ for which $g=f|_U:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$. Put $W=f^{-1}(V)$ with its open subscheme structure. Since $f(U)\subseteq V$, the inclusion of $U$ in $Y$ factors as the open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ followed by $W\hookrightarrow Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, lemma-birational-birational, alternative (2); formation of the restricted target

proof.text: The restriction $p=f|_W:W\to V$ is the base change of $f$ along $V\hookrightarrow X$, so it is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change](1). Define $s=j\circ g^{-1}:V\to W$. Then $p\circ s=g\circ g^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], this section is a closed immersion. Its underlying image is exactly $U$, since $g^{-1}$ is an isomorphism onto $U$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $U$ is therefore closed in $W$.

source.place: Tags 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), 01KT (lemma-section-immersion); separated-case shortening of the argument in Morphisms 0BAJ

proof.text: The subset $U$ is dense in $W$: any nonempty open subset of $W$ is a nonempty open subset of $Y$, since $W$ is open in $Y$, and hence meets the dense subset $U$. Since Step 2 makes $U$ closed in $W$, its closure is both $U$ and $W$, so $U=W$ as open subsets of $Y$. The associated open subschemes are identical, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Consequently $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is precisely $g:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$. The open $V$ was dense in $X$, which proves the assertion, including the empty-scheme case.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, conclusion; elementary density argument after the closed-section calculation
